explanation: Fires most often on ' year' in 'last year', but also on many unrelated tokens: 'as was', 'today's'/'day's', 'good' after 'especially/a', 'Wherever', code tokens (@memberOf, tensorflow). Apart from 'last year', strength is hard to predict.

A mixture with no shared theme: word-piece suffixes (Arizon-ans, transist-ors, foref-athers), number words after 'into/include' (two, three), digits inside IDs/URLs, HTML/code tokens (<div, post, MONTH, auto-generated), and assorted words.

A mixture: second parts of proper names (King Abdullah, New Yorker, Schumer), dotted Java/C# member and package names (.printStackTrace, .StoredProcedure, .AlertDialog, .psi), and some expressive adjectives/adverbs (silently, stifling, wrath, tremendous).

Fires on the assignment '=' in code and in algebra word problems ('[a,b] =', '... - 27 = 0'), and on 'by' in 'generated by' code headers. More weakly fires on name endings or commas after personal names in legal/author lists (Sanchez, Potencier, FRAISER).

Mostly fires at boundaries just after a title, heading or dateline (the '\n\n' after an article/Wikipedia title, ')' in 'DETROIT (WXYZ)', the year digit in an event title like '2007 World...'), plus some unrelated tokens (cook 'until', 'what', code casts). The boundary behaviour is common but loose.

A mixture: word pieces inside chemical/drug names (glut-, lact-, acet-, zot-), name fragments (Tu-areg, Tuilagi, Viz-ianagaram), license boilerplate ('BE LIABLE', 'DIRECT,'), and biographical words ('student at', 'attended'). No single trigger.

Fires on word pieces in the middle of rare proper names or technical terms that are split into subwords (Bous-man, Th-icke, Ph-yt-olacca, Vander-burgh, Ansar Al-Khilafah, Ras Al Kh-air), usually the first piece after the name starts. Common words fire only weakly.

Fires on middle word pieces of long words split into several tokens, especially in non-English (Portuguese, Danish, French, Spanish, German) or technical vocabulary (recom-enda-ção, er-stat-ninger, plurip-ot-ency, Aeron-aut-ics, JUD-G-MENT). It responds to pieces that continue a word, not to whole words.

A mixture: code tokens such as '.Support', ' (!', '#if HAVE', '(property', 'else if'; 'and' joining verbs or noun phrases in technical/patent prose; and assorted name or word-start pieces (NSF, Waterbury, LAKE, GLEW). No shared theme.

A mixture: word or path completions in URLs and code (bit.ly, bin/bash, PTR, SpatialReference, aliyunsdk), suffixes completing words (trans-locations, engr-ained, thorough-going), and common prose words ('a good idea', 'a lot', 'hint'). No clear common trigger.

Fires strongly on 'St' meaning Saint in place or institution names (St Paul's School, St. Stanislaus, Rector of St Alban's, [St. Louis). It also fires on word-internal pieces in Finnish, Romanian, Greek and other non-English text, and on a few other name pieces.

Fires on word pieces inside foreign or unusual proper names and non-English words (Sh-ann-ons, Eö-tv-ös, Ben-Gurion, Asgh-ar, Te-g-ucigalpa, Mark Ham-ill), usually an early piece just after the name starts. Common English words are weak.

A mixture: JSON/config keys and identifiers ('"type"', 'aws', add_section), suffixes in technical words (MRS, Accred-iting, deoxyribonucle-ic), and phrase completions in prose ('format possible', 'tip of', 'wrong feet', 'early form of').

A mixture: first letters or pieces of names and acronyms (D, MET, O-ta, G-abbard, Dextr, Div-el), single-letter literals in code ('A', <a), body-part nouns in sexual text (fingers, balls), and assorted nouns (header files, memory).

Mainly fires on future/modal 'will' after a subject or relative 'that' ('that will pay', 'he will reconsider', 'I will be') and on contractions after I ('I'll', 'I've'), so it tracks future or perfect auxiliaries. There are also unrelated hits on encoding artifacts ('xe2x80'-style digits), Java 'public', and '$.'.

A mixture: the verb or determiner right after a sentence subject ('program has', 'We have', 'It had', 'their'), 'genetic' or 'psychological' before study nouns, place-name pieces (Pet-aluma, Nittany), and code tokens ('=', 'components/').

A mixture of second pieces of split words: medical prefixes (ant-ie-pileptic, ant-ine-oplastic, nucle-os-ide), charset names in HTML meta tags (UTF, iso), license boilerplate words (Affero General, Licensed under, for linear algebra), and pieces of foreign words.

A mixture: second parts of compound code identifiers (php-complete, special-season, short-name, access_log, Weak-Set), punctuation in lists or paths, and assorted prose words (mortality, million, 'is that', 'straight').

A mixture: word-initial 'm' pieces (hit-and-miss, molar, mauling, mums), name pieces (Zel-az-ny, Doheny), and scientific prose nouns or modals (results, studies, observations, examination, may). No unifying feature.

Fires strongly on existential 'there'/'There' (there is/are/has been/might be), especially right after 'However,', 'Currently,', 'but' or 'that'. It fires moderately on presentational 'Here' ('Here are/is') and weakly on sentence-initial 'It'.

Fires on the final piece of a split name, completing it, especially 'ar' in names like Oskar and Asghar, and other endings of foreign or rare names (Ogh-am, af-ghan, Alban-ian, A-ar-ons). Weaker on endings of common compound words (undergar-ments, eBook, Aff-air).
